complete_source_units.text: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all Judah’s people in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah,
which he spoke to all Judah’s people and Jerusalem’s inhabitants, saying:
In the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amos, king of Judah, and until this day, twenty-three years, I spoke to you, rising early and saying,
and I was sending My servants the prophets to you, sending from early morning, and you did not listen or attend with your ears,
saying: Turn, each from his evil way and from your evil practices, and you will dwell upon the land I gave to you and your fathers from age to age.
Do not follow foreign gods to serve them and bow down to them, so that you do not provoke Me by your hands’ works into harming you.
And you did not hear Me.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Since you did not believe My words,

behold, I am sending and will take the clan from the north and bring them against this land, its inhabitants, and all the surrounding nations. I will lay them waste and make them a ruin, a hissing, and eternal reproach.
And I will remove from them the sound of joy and delight, the sound of bridegroom and bride, the fragrance of ointment and the light of a lamp.
And all the land will become a ruin, and they will serve among the nations for seventy years.
And when the seventy years are fulfilled, I will exact justice from that nation, says the Lord, and make them an everlasting ruin.
And I will bring upon that land all My words that I spoke against it, everything written in this book. What Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
What Jeremiah prophesied concerning the nations, Elam. At the beginning of King Zedekiah’s reign, this word came concerning Elam.
Thus says the Lord: Let Elam’s bow be shattered, the beginning of their dominion.
I will bring upon Elam four winds from heaven’s four ends and scatter them among all these winds. There will be no nation where Elam’s outcasts do not come.
I will terrify them before their enemies who seek their lives and bring calamities upon them according to the anger of My wrath. I will send My sword after them until they are consumed.
I will set My throne in Elam and send king and nobles away from there.
In the last days I will turn back Elam’s captivity, says the Lord.

For Egypt, concerning the force of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, who was beside the Euphrates River at Carchemish and whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim king of Judah:
Take up weapons and shields, and advance to war!
Saddle the horses; mount, riders! Take your positions in your helmets. Hold your spears forward; put on your breastplates!
Why are they terrified and withdrawing backward? Because their strong men will be cut down. They fled in flight and did not turn back, surrounded on every side, says the Lord.
Let the swift not flee, nor the strong man escape. Northward, in the places beside the Euphrates, they grew weak and have fallen.
Who is this who will rise like a river, and like rivers churn water?
Egypt’s waters will rise like a river, and it said, I will rise and cover the land and destroy those living in it.
Mount the horses; prepare the chariots! Go out, warriors of the Ethiopians and Libyans equipped with weapons! And Lydians, go up and draw the bow!

That day belongs to the Lord our God, a day of vengeance, to take vengeance on His enemies. The Lord’s sword will devour, be filled, and become drunk with their blood, for the Lord Sabaoth has a sacrifice from the northern land beside the Euphrates River.
Go up, Gilead, and take resin for the virgin daughter Egypt. In vain you multiplied your remedies; there is no benefit for you.
Nations heard your voice, and the land was filled with your cry, for warrior grew weak against warrior; both fell together.
What the Lord spoke through Jeremiah concerning Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon coming to cut down Egypt’s land:
Announce to Migdol and proclaim to Memphis. Say, Take your position and prepare, for the sword has devoured your smilax growth.
Why did Apis flee? Your choice calf did not remain, for the Lord disabled him.
Your multitude grew weak and fell, and each spoke to his neighbor, Let us rise and return to our people, to our homeland, away from the Greek sword.
Call Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt by the name Saon-esbi-emoeed.
As I live, says the Lord God, like Itabyrion among the mountains and Carmel in the sea, he will come.
Prepare belongings for deportation, resident daughter Egypt, for Memphis will become a ruin and will be called Woe because no inhabitants remain in her.
Egypt is a beautified heifer; a detachment from the north came against her.
Her hired men within her are like fattened calves being fed within her. They too turned and fled together; they did not stand, for a day of destruction came upon them, the time of their vengeance.
A sound like a hissing snake, for they will travel through sand; with axes they will come against her like woodcutters.
They will cut down her forest, says the Lord God, for it certainly cannot be estimated, for it multiplies beyond a locust swarm, and they are beyond numbering.
Daughter Egypt was put to shame, handed over to a people from the north.
I am taking vengeance for Amon her son upon Pharaoh and those who trust him.
But do not fear, My slave Jacob, nor be terrified, Israel, for I am saving you from afar and your offspring from their captivity. Jacob will return, be quiet, and sleep, and no one will trouble him.

Do not fear, My servant Jacob, says the Lord, for I am with you. I will make an end of every nation where I thrust you out, but I certainly will not make you perish. I will discipline you for judgment and certainly will not acquit you.
The Lord’s word that He spoke against Babylon:
Announce among the nations and make it heard; do not hide it. Say, Babylon has been captured! Bel was disgraced, the fearless one; the delicate one was handed over, Marodach.
A nation came up against her from the north; it will make her land a ruin, with no one living in it, from human to livestock.
In those days and at that time, Israel’s sons and Judah’s sons will come together; walking and weeping, they will go seeking the Lord their God.
They will ask the way as far as Zion, for they will turn their faces here. They will come and take refuge with the Lord God, for an everlasting covenant will not be forgotten.
My people became lost sheep; their shepherds thrust them away and led them astray upon the mountains. They went from mountain to hill and forgot their resting place.
All who found them consumed them. Their enemies said, Let us not release them, because they sinned against the Lord, the pasture of righteousness, who gathered their fathers.
Separate yourselves from Babylon’s midst and the Chaldeans’ land; come out and become like dragons before sheep.
I am rousing assemblies of nations against Babylon from the north. They will deploy against her; from there she will be captured. Like a discerning warrior’s missile, it will not return empty.
Chaldea will become plunder; all who plunder her will be filled.
because you rejoiced and boasted while plundering My inheritance, because you leaped like little cattle in pasture and butted like bulls,
your mother was deeply ashamed—a mother for good things, last of nations, a wilderness.
Because of the Lord’s anger she will not be inhabited and will entirely disappear. Everyone passing through Babylon will look gloomy, and they will hiss at every wound of hers.
Deploy against Babylon all around, all who stretch the bow. Shoot at her; do not spare your arrows.
Clap against her! Her hands were disabled, her battlements fell, and her wall was demolished. For this is vengeance from God; take vengeance upon her. Do to her as she did.
Destroy seed from Babylon, the one holding a sickle at harvest. Before the Greek sword, each will return to his people and flee to his land.
Israel is a wandering sheep driven away by lions. First Assyria’s king ate him; later this one, Babylon’s king, ate his bones.
Therefore thus says the Lord: I am taking vengeance upon Babylon’s king and his land, as I took vengeance upon Assyria’s king.
I will restore Israel to his pasture. He will graze on Carmel, on Ephraim’s mountain, and in Gilead, and his soul will be filled.

In those days and at that time they will seek Israel’s injustice, and it will not exist, and Judah’s sins, and they certainly will not be found, for I will be merciful to those left upon the land, says the Lord.
Go fiercely against her and her inhabitants. Take vengeance, sword, and make her disappear, says the Lord; do everything I command you.
A sound of war and great shattering in the Chaldeans’ land!
How the hammer of the whole earth was snapped and shattered! How Babylon became a ruin among nations!
They will attack you and you will be captured, Babylon, without knowing it. You were found and taken because you resisted the Lord.
The Lord opened His treasury and brought out the instruments of His anger, for the Lord God has work in the Chaldeans’ land,
for her times have arrived. Open her storehouses; search her like a cave and destroy her. Let no remnant of her remain.
Dry up all her fruits, and let them go down to slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their vengeance.
A sound of those fleeing and being rescued from Babylon’s land, announcing in Zion vengeance from the Lord our God!

Give orders against Babylon to many, to everyone drawing a bow. Encamp against her all around; let none of her people escape. Repay her according to her works; do to her all she did, for she resisted the Lord, Israel’s holy God.
Therefore her young men will fall in her squares, and all her warriors will be thrown down, said the Lord.
I am against you, insolent woman, says the Lord, for your day has come, the time of your vengeance.
Your insolence will grow weak and fall, with no one to raise it. I will kindle fire in her forest, and it will devour everything around her.
Thus says the Lord: Israel’s sons and Judah’s sons have been oppressed together. All who captured them oppressed them, because they did not want to release them.
The One redeeming them is strong; the Lord Almighty is His name. He will judge a case against His adversaries, to remove the land, and He will provoke Babylon’s inhabitants.
A sword against the Chaldeans, Babylon’s inhabitants, her nobles, and her discerning men!
A sword against her warriors, and they will be disabled!
A sword against their horses and chariots! A sword against their warriors and the mixed people within her, and they will become like women! A sword against her treasures, and they will be scattered!
She trusted in her water, and they will be ashamed, for it is a land of carved images, and in the islands where they boasted.
Therefore apparitions will live on the islands, and daughters of sirens will live in her. She certainly will never again be inhabited.
As God overturned Sodom, Gomorrah, and their bordering places, said the Lord, no person will live there, and no human being will reside there.
A people is coming from the north; a great nation and many kings will be roused from the earth’s farthest part,
holding bow and dagger. It is insolent and certainly will not show mercy. Their voice will sound like the sea. They will ride horses, prepared like fire for war against you, daughter Babylon.
Babylon’s king heard the report about them, and his hands were disabled. Distress seized him, birth pains like a woman giving birth.

Like a lion he will come up from the Jordan into Aitham’s place, for I will quickly drive them away from her and appoint every young man over her. For who is like Me? Who will resist Me, and what shepherd can stand before Me?

Therefore hear the Lord’s counsel that He has planned against Babylon and His purposes against the resident Chaldeans: Surely the lambs of their sheep will be destroyed; surely pasture will disappear from them.
For at the sound of Babylon’s capture the earth will shake, and a cry will be heard among the nations.
Thus says the Lord: I am rousing a destroying hot wind against Babylon and against the Chaldeans who live there.
I will send insolent men to Babylon; they will abuse her and ravage her land. Woe upon Babylon all around on the day of her affliction!
Against her let the archer stretch his bow, and let the man who has armor put it on. Do not spare her young men; obliterate her whole force.
Wounded men will fall in the Chaldeans’ land, and pierced men outside her.
For Israel and Judah have not been widowed of their God, of the Lord Almighty, because their land was filled with injustice from Israel’s holy ones.
Flee from Babylon’s midst; each of you save your life. Do not be cast away in her injustice, for her time of vengeance is from the Lord; He is repaying her recompense.
Babylon was a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, making the whole earth drunk. Nations drank her wine; therefore they were shaken.
Suddenly Babylon fell and was shattered. Lament her! Take resin for her corruption, if somehow she may be healed.
We treated Babylon, but she was not healed. Let us leave her; let each of us go to our own land, for her judgment reached heaven and rose to the stars.
The Lord has brought forth His judgment. Come, let us announce in Zion the works of the Lord our God.
Prepare the arrows; fill the quivers. The Lord roused the spirit of the Medes’ king, for His anger against Babylon is to destroy her. This is the Lord’s vengeance, vengeance for His people.
Raise a signal on Babylon’s walls; set up quivers, raise guards, prepare weapons, for the Lord has undertaken and will do what He spoke against Babylon’s inhabitants,
who dwell beside many waters and her abundance of treasures. Your end has truly come to your inward parts.
For the Lord swore by His arm: I will fill you with people like locusts, and those coming down will speak out against you.
He makes the earth by His strength, prepares the inhabited world by His wisdom, and stretched out heaven by His understanding.
At His voice He set a sound of water in heaven and brought clouds up from the earth’s end. He made lightning for rain and brought light out of His treasuries.
Every person became foolish, without knowledge; every goldsmith was disgraced by his carvings, because they cast false things, and there is no spirit in them.
They are vain, mocked works; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
Jacob’s portion is not like this, for the One who formed all things is Himself his inheritance. The Lord is His name.
You scatter instruments of war for Me. In you I will scatter nations, and from you I will remove kings.
In you I will scatter horse and rider; in you I will scatter chariots and their riders.
In you I will scatter young man and virgin; in you I will scatter man and woman.
In you I will scatter shepherd and flock; in you I will scatter farmer and farmland; in you I will scatter your leaders and generals.
I will repay Babylon and all the Chaldeans who live there for all the evils they did against Zion before your eyes, says the Lord.
I am against you, ruined mountain that ruins the whole earth. I will stretch My hand against you, roll you down from the rocks, and make you like a burned mountain.
They will certainly not take from you a cornerstone or a foundation stone, for you will be a ruin for ever, says the Lord.

Raise a signal on the earth; sound a trumpet among the nations. Consecrate nations against her; give orders against her to Ararat’s kingdoms from Me and to the Ashkenazites. Set up arrow batteries against her; bring up horses against her like a multitude of locusts.
Consecrate nations against her: the king of the Medes and of all the earth, his leaders and all his generals.
The earth was shaken and suffered, for the Lord’s purpose rose against Babylon, to make Babylon’s land a ruin, no longer inhabited.
Babylon’s warrior has ceased fighting; they will sit there in confinement. Their power was crushed; they became like women. Her dwellings were burned; her bars were shattered.
Pursuer will pursue to meet pursuer, and announcer to meet announcer, to tell Babylon’s king that his city has been captured;
from the extremity of his crossings they were taken, and their gatherings were burned with fire, and his warriors are going out.
For thus says the Lord: The houses of Babylon’s king will be threshed like a threshing floor ready for use; a little longer, and her harvest will come.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon devoured me, divided me, seized me, a thin vessel. He swallowed me like a dragon, filled his belly, and drove me from my luxury.
My toils and miseries be upon Babylon, the woman dwelling in Zion will say; my blood be upon the Chaldeans who live there, Jerusalem will say.
Therefore thus says the Lord: I will judge your adversary and avenge you; I will lay her sea waste and dry her spring.
Babylon will become a ruin and will not be inhabited.
Together they were roused like lions and like lions’ cubs.
In their heat I will give them a drink and make them drunk, so that they are stupefied and sleep an everlasting sleep and certainly do not rise, says the Lord.
I will bring them down like lambs to slaughter and like rams with young goats.
How the boast of the whole earth was captured and hunted! How Babylon became a ruin among the nations!
The sea rose over Babylon with the sound of its waves, and she was covered.
Her cities became a waterless and untrodden land; not one person will live there, nor will any human lodge there.
I will exact vengeance on Babylon and bring what she swallowed out of her mouth. Nations will certainly no longer gather to her.
And in Babylon wounded men from all the earth will fall.
You who escape from the land, go on; do not stand still. You who are far away, remember the Lord, and let Jerusalem rise in your hearts.
We were disgraced, for we heard our reproach; dishonor covered our face. Foreigners entered our holy places, the Lord’s house.
Therefore days are coming, says the Lord, when I will exact vengeance on her carvings, and wounded men will fall throughout her land.
Even if Babylon rises as high as heaven and fortifies the height of her strength, those who destroy her will come from Me, says the Lord.
A sound of crying in Babylon, a great shattering in the Chaldeans’ land!
For the Lord destroyed Babylon and silenced her loud voice sounding like many waters; He gave her voice over to destruction.
For misery came upon Babylon. Her warriors were captured; their bow is terrified, because God repays them; the Lord repays her recompense.
He will make her leaders and wise men and generals thoroughly drunk, says the King, whose name is the Lord Almighty.
Thus says the Lord: Babylon’s wall was broadened; it will be utterly demolished, and her high gates burned. Peoples will not labor in vain, and nations will perish at the beginning.

The word the Lord commanded Jeremiah the prophet to tell Seraiah son of Neriah son of Maaseiah when he went from Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was an official over gifts.
Jeremiah wrote in one scroll all the evils that would come upon Babylon, all these words written against Babylon.
Jeremiah said to Seraiah: When you arrive in Babylon, you will see and read all these words,
and say, Lord, Lord, Thou spakest against this place to destroy it and leave no inhabitants in it, from human to livestock, for it will be a ruin for ever.
When you finish reading this scroll, bind a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates,
and say, Thus Babylon will sink and certainly not rise because of the evils I am bringing upon her.
Concerning the people of another tribe.

Thus says the Lord: Waters are rising from the north and will become a flooding torrent. It will flood the land and its fullness, the city and those living in it. People will cry out, and all the land’s inhabitants will shout aloud.
At the sound of his onrush, of the hooves of his feet, the shaking of his chariots, and the noise of his wheels, fathers did not turn back to their sons, because their hands failed,
on the day coming to destroy all the people of another tribe. I will obliterate Tyre and Sidon and all the remainder of their assistance, for the Lord will destroy the survivors of the islands.
Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon and the survivors of the Anakim have been cast away. How long will you strike,
sword of the Lord? How long will you not be quiet? Return to your sheath; rest and be lifted away!
How will it be quiet? The Lord commanded it to rise against Ashkelon, against the coastal places, against those remaining.
For Idumea, thus says the Lord: There is no longer wisdom in Teman; counsel perished from the discerning; their wisdom went away.
Their place was deceived. Go deep to dwell, inhabitants of Dedan, for he did difficult things; I brought them upon him at the time I visited him.
For grape gatherers came to you; they will leave you no remnants. Like thieves by night they will lay their hand upon you.
For I dragged Esau away and uncovered their secrets; they certainly cannot hide. They perished by the hand of his brother and his neighbor, and it is not possible
for your orphan to remain so that he may live. And I will live, and widows have trusted in Me.
For thus said the Lord: Those for whom there was no law to drink the cup drank it. And you, though acquitted, certainly will not be acquitted, for you will certainly drink.
For I swore by Myself, says the Lord, that you will become an untrodden place, a reproach, and a curse in her midst, and all her cities will be deserted for ever.
I heard a report from the Lord, and He sent messengers to the nations: Gather and come against her; rise for war!
I made you small among nations, easily despised among people.
Your playfulness assailed you; your heart’s insolence destroyed holes in rocks and seized the strength of a high hill. For he raised his nest like an eagle; from there I will bring you down.
Idumea will become an untrodden place; everyone passing by her will hiss.
As Sodom, Gomorrah, and her neighboring places were overturned, said the Lord Almighty, no person will settle there, and no human being will live there.

Like a lion he will come up from Jordan’s midst into Aitham’s place, for I will quickly drive them away from her. Appoint the young men over her. For who is like Me? Who will resist Me, and what shepherd can stand before Me?

Therefore hear the Lord’s counsel that He planned against Idumea and His purpose against Teman’s inhabitants: Surely the smallest sheep will be swept together; surely their dwelling will be made untrodden over her.
For at the sound of their fall the earth shook, and your cry was heard at the sea.
Like an eagle he will look and stretch his wings over her fortifications. That day Idumea’s strong men’s hearts will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
For Ammon’s sons, thus said the Lord: Are there no sons in Israel, or have they no one to inherit? Why did Melchom take Gad, and will their people live in their cities?

Therefore days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make the din of wars heard against Rabbath. They will become an untrodden place and a destruction, her altars will be burned with fire, and Israel will receive his rule.

Shout aloud, Heshbon, for Gai perished! Cry out, daughters of Rabbath; put on sackcloth, be seized with distress, and beat yourselves over Melchom, for he will go into deportation, his priests and rulers together.
Why do you exult in the plains of the Anakim, daughter of dishonor, trusting in her treasures and saying, Who will come against me?
I am bringing fear upon you, said the Lord, from all your surroundings. You will be scattered, each straight ahead, and there will be no one gathering.
For Kedar, queen of the courtyard, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. Thus said the Lord: Rise and go up against Kedar, and fill the sons of Kedem!
They will take their tents and sheep, their garments, all their equipment, and camels for themselves. Call destruction against them on every side!
Flee far away; go deep to dwell, you who stay in the courtyard, for Babylon’s king planned counsel against you and devised a purpose against you.
Rise and go up against a stable nation living in refreshment, with neither doors nor pins nor bars; they lodge alone.

Their camels will become plunder and their numerous livestock destruction. I will winnow them to every wind, those shorn before their faces; from every side of them I will bring their rout, said the Lord.
The courtyard will become an abode for ostriches, untrodden for ever. No person will settle there; no human being will live there.
For Damascus: Hamath and Arpad were ashamed because they heard an evil report. They were distraught and angry; they certainly cannot rest.
Damascus grew feeble and turned to flight; trembling seized her.
How did he not abandon My city? They loved a village.
Therefore young men will fall in your squares, and all your warriors will fall, says the Lord.
I will kindle fire in Damascus’s wall, and it will devour the quarters of Ader’s son.
For Moab, thus said the Lord: Woe to Nebo, for she perished! Kiriathaim was taken; Amath was disgraced and defeated.
There is no longer healing for Moab, a boast in Heshbon. They devised evils against her: We cut her off from a nation, and she will certainly cease. A sword will walk behind you.
For a sound of people crying out comes from Horonaim: destruction and great shattering!
Moab was shattered; announce it in Zogora.
For Alaoth was filled with weeping; he will go up weeping on Horonaim’s road. You heard a cry of shattering:
Flee and save your lives, and you will be like a wild donkey in the wilderness!
Because you trusted in your fortifications, you too will be seized. Chemosh will go into deportation, his priests and rulers together.
Destruction will come upon every city; no city will be saved. The valley will perish and the plain be destroyed, as the Lord said.
Give signs to Moab, for she will surely be kindled; all her cities will become an untrodden place. From where will an inhabitant come to her?
Accursed is one who does the Lord’s works carelessly, removing his sword from blood.
Moab rested from childhood and trusted in his glory. He did not pour from vessel to vessel or go into deportation. Therefore his taste remained in him and his scent did not fade.
Therefore days are coming, says the Lord, when I will send him tilters who will tip him, thin out his vessels, and cut up his horns.
Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as Israel’s house was ashamed of Bethel, their hope, having trusted in them.
How will you say, We are strong, and a man strong for warfare?
Moab perished, his city, and his choice young men went down to slaughter.
Moab’s day is near to coming, and his calamity is very swift.
Move in lament for him, all who surround him, all who know his name. Say, How the renowned staff is shattered, the rod of grandeur!
Come down from glory and sit in dampness, resident Dibon. Be crushed, for Moab perished; he came up against you, ruining your fortification.
Stand on the road and look, you who live in Aroer. Ask the one fleeing and the one being saved, and say, What happened?
Moab was ashamed, for he was shattered. Wail and cry out; announce at Arnon that Moab perished.
Judgment is coming into the land of Misor: upon Chailon, Jahzah, and Mophath,
upon Dibon, Nebo, and the house of Deblathaim,
upon Kiriathaim, the house of Gamol, and the house of Maon,
upon Kerioth, Bosor, and all Moab’s cities, far and near.
Moab’s horn was broken and his effort shattered.
Make him drunk, for he magnified himself against the Lord. Moab will strike with his hand and become a laughingstock himself.
Was not Israel a laughingstock to you? Was he found in your thefts, that you made war on him?
Moab’s inhabitants left the cities and lived among rocks. They became like doves nesting among rocks at a pit’s mouth.
I heard Moab’s insolence; he acted very insolently—his insolence and arrogance—and his heart was lifted up.
But I knew his works. Not his sufficiency; he did not act so.
Therefore wail over Moab from every side; cry out over the men of Kiradas of drought.
Like the weeping for Jazer, I will weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Your branches crossed the sea and reached Jazer. Destruction fell upon your summer fruit and your grape gatherers.
Joy and gladness were boiled away from Moab’s land, and wine was upon your winepresses. They did not tread in the morning or in the evening; they did not make an aidad shout.
From Heshbon’s cry as far as Elealeh, their cities raised their voice; from Zogor to Horonaim and Aglath-salisia, for even Nebrim’s water will become a burning.
I will destroy Moab, says the Lord, as he goes up to an altar and burns incense to his gods.
Therefore my heart, Moab, will hum like flutes; my heart will hum like a flute for Kiradas’s people. Therefore what he acquired perished from a person.
They will shave every head in every place; every beard will be shaved, all hands will beat themselves, and on every waist is sackcloth.
And on all Moab’s rooftops and in her squares—for I shattered Moab, says the Lord, like a vessel for which there is no use.
How he has changed! How Moab turned his back! He was ashamed, and Moab became a laughingstock and an object of resentment to all around her.
For thus said the Lord:
Akkarioth was taken and the fortifications seized.
Moab will perish from being a multitude, for he magnified himself against the Lord.
Trap, fear, and pit are upon you, resident Moab.
One who flees from fear will fall into the pit, and one who climbs from the pit will be caught in the trap, for I will bring these things upon Moab in the year of her visitation.
Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Take this cup of unmixed wine from My hand, and give it to all the nations to whom I send you to drink,
and they will drink, vomit, and go mad before the sword I am sending among them.
And I took the cup from the Lord’s hand and gave it to the nations to whom the Lord sent me to drink:
Jerusalem, Judah’s cities, Judah’s kings, and its rulers, to make them a desolation, an untrodden place, and a hissing;
and Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his nobles, and all his people;
and all his mixed population, all the Philistine kings, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and Ashdod’s remnant;
and Idumea, the Moabite land, and Ammon’s sons;
and all Tyre’s kings, Sidon’s kings, and the kings across the sea;
and Dedan, Teman, Ros, and everyone shorn about his face;
and all the mixed populations lodging in the wilderness;
and all Elam’s kings and all the Persian kings;
and all the kings from the east, far and near, each with his brother, and all the kingdoms upon the face of the earth.
And say to them: Thus said the Lord Almighty: Drink, get drunk, and vomit; you will fall and certainly not rise before the sword I am sending among you.
And when they are unwilling to receive the cup from your hand to drink, say: Thus said the Lord: You will certainly drink.
Because I am beginning to bring harm in the city upon which My name was named, and you will certainly not be cleansed, because I am summoning a sword against those dwelling upon the earth.

And prophesy these words against them and say: The Lord will give an oracle from on high; from His holy place He will raise His voice. He will give an oracular word over His place, and they will answer with Aidad, like grape-gatherers. And upon those dwelling upon the earth,
destruction comes upon a part of the earth, because the Lord has a judgment among the nations. He enters judgment with all flesh, and the ungodly were given to the sword, says the Lord.
Thus said the Lord: Behold, evils come from nation to nation, and a great whirlwind goes out from the earth’s farthest end.
And those wounded by the Lord on the Lord’s day will lie from one part of the earth to another. They will certainly not be buried; they will be dung upon the earth’s face.
Raise a shout, shepherds, and cry out; beat yourselves in mourning, rams of the sheep, because your days for slaughter have been fulfilled, and you will fall like choice rams.
And flight will perish from the shepherds, and salvation from the rams of the sheep.
A sound of shepherds crying and of sheep and rams shouting, because the Lord destroyed their grazing places,
and the remnants of peace will cease before the anger of My fury.
Like a lion He abandoned His lodging, because their land became an untrodden place before the great sword.
